channel.title: Toyota recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Toyota RAV4, Tundra Hybrid Weight Label Error
item.description: The label on your vehicle that shows the load carrying capacity modification may display an inaccurate added weight value. This means the number telling you how much extra weight your vehicle can carry may not be correct. Dealers will replace the load carrying capacity modification label with a corrected one, free of charge, once new labels are ready to be mailed to owners.

item.title: Camry Hybrid Cluster Failure Disables Warning Lights
item.description: Some 2025-2026 Camry Hybrid vehicles may have an instrument cluster display that fails to work when the vehicle is started. If that happens, the hazard lights, turn signals, seat belt warning system, and smart key reminder can all be deactivated at the same time.

item.title: Toyota Tacoma Shock Absorber Reservoir Can Detach
item.description: On some Toyota Tacoma vehicles, a metal flange on the front and rear shock absorbers may corrode. If it corrodes enough to fail, the external oil reservoir attached to the shock absorber can detach from the vehicle.

item.title: Toyota Land Cruiser Hybrid Dashboard Warnings May Fail
item.description: The instrument panel display in these vehicles, which normally shows warning lights and gauges, may fail to show certain warnings or indicators to the driver. This means information such as engine coolant temperature or the vehicle's electrical charge level might not appear on the dashboard when it should, so a driver may not see an important warning while driving.

item.title: Toyota Tundra Engine Bearing Failure May Cause Stall
item.description: On certain Tundra vehicles with a V35A engine, debris left over from manufacturing may contaminate the engine and cause a main bearing to fail. This can cause the engine to stall and the vehicle to lose drive power. Dealers will inspect the engine using diagnostic software and drive data, and will replace the engine if necessary, free of charge.

item.title: Toyota RAV4 Front Seat Brackets Welded Improperly
item.description: Some 2025 RAV4s have front seat brackets on the seat rails that may not be welded correctly.

item.title: Toyota Corolla Cross Hybrid backup warning sound too quiet
item.description: Toyota is recalling certain Corolla Cross Hybrid vehicles because they may not make a loud enough warning sound for pedestrians when backing up. Hybrid and electric vehicles are required by federal rules to make a minimum amount of sound so people nearby can hear them, and these vehicles do not meet that requirement. Dealers will update the software that controls the pedestrian warning sound at no cost. Owner letters were mailed September 1, 2026.

item.title: Toyota and Lexus vehicles have incorrect weight capacity labels
item.description: Toyota is recalling certain Toyota and Lexus trucks, SUVs and hybrid models. The load carrying capacity modification label, which lists how much added weight the vehicle can carry, may show inaccurate values. Because of that, these vehicles do not meet the federal safety standard covering tire selection and rims. Dealers will replace the label free of charge, and Toyota mailed owner letters on May 26, 2026.

item.title: Toyota Highlander second-row seat back may not lock
item.description: This recall covers certain Toyota Highlander and Highlander Hybrid vehicles. The second-row seat backs may fail to lock into position when the seat back is being adjusted.

item.title: BMW, Toyota Supra: Engine Starter May Catch Fire
item.description: On affected vehicles, the engine starter may overheat and catch fire due to wear on an internal component.

item.title: Toyota Prius Rear Door May Open While Driving
item.description: Toyota is recalling certain Prius, Prius Prime, and Prius Plug-in Hybrid vehicles because water may get into the rear door switch and cause a short circuit. This can cause an unlocked rear door to open unexpectedly while the vehicle is being driven.

item.title: Toyota Tundra rearview camera image may not show
item.description: Certain Tundra and Tundra Hybrid trucks have a Panoramic View Monitor camera system. On these vehicles, the rearview camera image may not display when the truck is shifted into reverse. Toyota is recalling the affected vehicles to update the parking assist control unit's software so the camera image displays as intended when backing up.

item.title: Honda, Chrysler and Toyota Vans Wheelchair Restraint Issue
item.description: Some vehicles equipped with certain wheelchair restraint systems have retractors that may not lock properly. This means a wheelchair might not be securely held in place while the vehicle is being driven. Dealers will inspect the retractors and replace them if needed, free of charge.

item.title: Wheelchair Restraints in Various Vehicles May Not Lock
item.description: Certain vehicles equipped with QRT-Deluxe or QRT-Max wheelchair restraints may have retractors that fail to lock. If the retractor does not lock, a wheelchair inside the vehicle may not be properly secured.

item.title: Toyota Highlander Third-Row Seat Belt Anchor Defect
item.description: Some Highlander and Highlander Hybrid vehicles may have the third-row center seat belt's roof anchor installed at an incorrect angle. This can prevent the seat belt from properly restraining the occupant.

item.title: Toyota Camry Hybrid inverter fault risks power loss
item.description: In some Camry Hybrid and Corolla Cross Hybrid vehicles, a bolt inside the inverter may not have been tightened properly. This can cause incomplete contact at one of the inverter's terminals. Incomplete contact can cause the vehicle to lose motive power while driving. A loose bolt can also cause an electrical short while the vehicle is powered on, which increases the risk of a fire.

item.title: Toyota Tundra Engine May Stall From Bearing Failure
item.description: Debris left over from the manufacturing process may contaminate the engine, which can cause the main bearings inside the engine to fail. If a main bearing fails, the engine can stall and the vehicle can lose the power that turns the wheels. This can happen while the vehicle is being driven, leaving the driver without the ability to keep the vehicle moving under its own power.

item.title: Toyota, Lexus and Subaru rearview camera may freeze
item.description: Toyota is recalling certain 2022 through 2026 Toyota and Lexus vehicles and the Subaru Solterra that have the Panoramic View Monitor camera system. Models include RAV4, Highlander, Prius, Sienna Hybrid, Camry Hybrid, Mirai, bZ4X and the Lexus NX and TX Hybrid. A software error can cause the backup camera picture to freeze or go blank when the car is in reverse, so these vehicles do not meet the federal rear visibility standard.

item.title: Toyota Sienna Hybrid Second-Row Seat Rails Flawed
item.description: Toyota is recalling certain Sienna Hybrid vehicles because the rails that hold the second-row seats in place may have been welded incorrectly. A seat rail that is not welded properly may not hold the seat securely in a crash. If the seat cannot properly restrain the person sitting in it during a crash, that person has a higher chance of being injured.

item.title: Toyota Tacoma Front Driveshaft Can Break
item.description: The front driveshaft on your Tacoma has a joint that can bend out of shape and break over time. If it breaks, it can make the truck harder to steer. On trucks with full-time four-wheel drive, a broken driveshaft could also let the truck roll away on its own if it's parked without the parking brake applied. Toyota is recalling these trucks to check the front driveshaft joints for this problem.

item.title: Toyota Tundra, Sequoia Hybrid: Rearview Camera May Fail
item.description: A software error may cause the rearview camera image not to appear on the screen when the vehicle is shifted into reverse.

item.title: BMW and Toyota Supra Starter Relay Fire Risk
item.description: Certain BMW X3, X4, Z4, and Toyota Supra vehicles have an engine starter relay that can corrode over time. Once corroded, the relay may overheat and short circuit. This electrical problem can increase the risk of a fire, whether the vehicle is being driven or is already parked.

item.title: Toyota Instrument Panel May Fail To Show Warnings
item.description: A software error in the instrument panel can occur when the vehicle starts up. Because of this, the panel may fail to show the vehicle's speed, brake system warning, and tire pressure warning lights. This is happening on a range of Toyota models covered by this recall. The recall is being carried out in phases, with owner notification letters sent out in stages, and additional letters expected in the future.

item.title: Toyota bZ4X and Subaru Solterra Defroster May Fail
item.description: On some bZ4X and Solterra electric vehicles, certain HVAC system faults, such as the electric compressor failing, can cause the windshield defroster and defogger system to stop working. This can happen under certain driving conditions.

item.title: Toyota Tundra Reverse Light Failure From Moisture
item.description: In these Toyota Tundra and Tundra Hybrid vehicles, moisture may get inside the reverse light assemblies. If moisture enters these lights, it can cause the reverse lights to fail and stop working properly. This means the reverse lights, which are supposed to come on when the vehicle is shifted into reverse, may not work the way they should.

item.title: Toyota Sienna Third-Row Seat Bolts Loose
item.description: On certain Toyota Sienna Hybrid vehicles, the bolts holding the third-row seatback assemblies in place may not have been tightened properly. Because of this, these seats do not meet federal safety standards covering head restraints, seating systems, and child restraint anchors.

item.title: Toyota Tacoma rear brake hoses may leak fluid
item.description: On some 2024-2025 Toyota Tacoma 4-wheel drive vehicles, mud and dirt can build up inside the rear wheels and damage the rear brake hoses. This damage can cause a brake fluid leak. A brake fluid leak can reduce the vehicle's braking ability, meaning it could take longer to stop. Dealers will replace both rear brake hoses, free of charge.

item.title: Toyota Camry Hybrid Rear Center Seat Belt Damage
item.description: The webbing on the second-row center seat belt may be damaged. A damaged seat belt may not hold an occupant securely in place during a crash.

item.title: Toyota And Lexus Steering Defect Disables Airbag
item.description: These Toyota and Lexus vehicles may have been incorrectly repaired under an earlier recall for the same part. Inside the steering column there is an electrical connection that may not be welded well enough, and if it comes apart, the driver's airbag can turn off. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet a federal safety standard for protecting occupants in a crash.

item.title: Toyota Camry Low-Pressure Fuel Pump May Fail
item.description: On certain Camry vehicles, the low-pressure fuel pump inside the fuel tank may fail. If the pump fails, the engine can stall.

item.title: Toyota RAV4: Loose Front Brake and Wheel Bolts
item.description: Some bolts that hold the front brake caliper and wheel bearing in place may be loose. A loose bolt can damage a brake hose, causing a fluid leak that reduces braking performance, or it can let a wheel come loose from the vehicle. Either problem raises the chance of a crash.

item.title: Toyota Corolla Steering Shaft May Crack And Detach
item.description: Some Toyota Corolla and Corolla Hybrid vehicles may have a steering intermediate shaft that develops cracks during the manufacturing process. Over time, the shaft may fracture and possibly detach from the steering column, so it no longer connects properly. Dealers will replace the intermediate steering shaft to fix this, at no cost to owners. Toyota has already mailed notification letters to owners about this issue.

item.title: Toyota Tundra and Sequoia Tires May Lose Air
item.description: Toyota is recalling certain Sequoia Hybrid, Tundra, and Tundra Hybrid vehicles. The passenger-side front and rear tires may have damage on the inner sidewall, which can cause a sudden loss of tire pressure. To fix this, dealers will inspect the tires on affected vehicles and replace any tires that show this damage. This inspection and any needed tire replacement will be done at no cost to the vehicle owner.

item.title: Toyota Corolla Hybrid Brake Assist Software Error
item.description: A software error in the computer that controls your vehicle's skid control and braking system can cause a loss of power brake assist when you turn a corner. Power brake assist is the system that reduces the effort needed to press the brake pedal.

item.title: Toyota Sequoia Hybrid Tow Hitch Cover May Detach
item.description: Certain Sequoia Hybrid SUVs have a tow hitch cover attached to the rear bumper. Toyota says this cover may come loose from the bumper and detach from the vehicle while it's being driven. Once it comes off, the cover is left behind on the road as a loose piece separated from the vehicle, rather than staying attached where it belongs.

item.title: Toyota accessory weight label may show wrong numbers
item.description: Gulf States Toyota is recalling certain Toyota vehicles, mostly from the 2023 through 2025 model years, that were fitted with Gulf States Toyota accessories. Models include 4Runner, Corolla, Highlander, Prius, Tacoma, Tundra, Grand Highlander, Sequoia Hybrid, bZ4X, Venza Hybrid and others. The sticker that lists how much weight the added accessories take up may show wrong numbers, so these vehicles do not meet the federal standard for tire and rim selection.

item.title: Toyota and Lexus SUV curtain airbags may deploy wrong
item.description: Certain Toyota Grand Highlander and Lexus TX vehicles have driver and passenger side curtain air bags that may not unroll the way they are supposed to. Instead of deploying properly to protect occupants, the air bag could partially deploy outside of an open window. This means that in a crash, the air bag may not be positioned correctly to help protect the people inside the vehicle.

item.title: Toyota Highlander Accessory Tires Rated Too Low
item.description: Southeast Toyota Distributors says some Highlander vehicles came with 20-inch accessory tires that aren't rated to carry as much weight as these vehicles need. Because the tires' weight rating is too low for the vehicle, they could end up carrying more weight than they were built to handle. This means the vehicles don't meet a federal safety standard for tire selection.

item.title: Toyota Highlander Blackout Package Tires Underrated
item.description: Certain Highlander L and LE models built with the Blackout Package's 20-inch black alloy wheels were fitted with tires that do not have a high enough load rating for the vehicle. This means those tires are not rated to safely carry the weight they may need to carry on these vehicles.

item.title: Toyota Tundra Engine May Stall From Debris
item.description: Some Tundra and Lexus LX600 vehicles with a V35A engine may have debris left over from the manufacturing process inside the engine. This debris can contaminate the engine and cause the main bearings to fail. If that happens, the engine can stall while you're driving, and the vehicle can lose the power it needs to keep moving forward.
